author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces
summary: Reinstate the machine-readable veterinarian list as a supported surface and add an optional specialty filter to both the directory page and the machine-readable list: only veterinarians holding the named specialty are returned.
acceptance_criteria: Requested with no specialty, the machine-readable veterinarian list returns the full directory as a supported surface.
For a specialty one or more veterinarians hold, both the directory page and the machine-readable list return only those veterinarians; the page still lists them a page at a time.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and disregards letter case; a specialty name differing only by case matches, and only the start of a name does not match.
A specialty no veterinarian holds returns an empty directory in the normal structure on both surfaces, not an error.
An empty or whitespace-only specialty is treated as no filter and the full directory is returned, matching the empty owner-search precedent.
With no specialty asked for, both surfaces behave exactly as before this requirement.
Following a page-navigation link on a filtered directory page carries the same specialty so the next page stays filtered.
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search remains out of scope (NG-9, narrowed)
No on-screen specialty control — form, dropdown, or link — is added; a visible control may be a follow-up request
Filtering by attributes other than specialty, or filtering entities other than veterinarians
Behavior for a repeated or multi-valued specialty parameter is left unspecified
notes: Narrows NG-9 per adr/2026-08-24-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused; the machine-readable surface is now supported under REQ-VET-003. The ADR index at docs/adr/README.md needs a row for the new non-goal ADR (outside product-requirements-expert write scope).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fresh ground built on established patterns. The specialty filter is a Spring Data derived query on VetRepository (grep confirms the declarative repository and the two @Cacheable findAll methods; owner search's findByLastNameStartingWith is the sibling precedent). New because it reinstates the machine-readable /vets surface as a supported contract (retiring a Known-Defects row), adds a query-parameter filter mechanism absent from the vet surfaces today, and changes the vetList.html pagination-link contract to carry the filter. Contracts Implements columns for VetController, VetRepository, and Vets now cite REQ-VET-003 (docs/system-design.md#contracts). The how is recorded in adr/2026-08-24-specialty-filter-realization.md.
integration_points: VetRepository gains findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) for the HTML surface and a List-returning sibling for the machine-readable surface; leave both UNCACHED (only the full-list findAll reads stay @Cacheable).

VetController: both /vets.html and /vets read an optional @RequestParam specialty; the controller strips it and treats blank/whitespace as no-filter, branching to the existing findAll path (mirrors OwnerController.processFindForm lines 98-104).
VetController adds the active filter to the HTML model (the normalized value when filtering, null when absent) so the view can carry it on pagination links.

vetList.html pagination anchors move from the string-concatenated @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} form to Thymeleaf's parameter form @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}; a null specialty is omitted from the URL, keeping the no-filter URLs byte-identical to today.

patterns.description: empty/whitespace search precedent: strip the param, treat blank as the broadest result, keep paging at the repository. Vet blank differs in one respect — it routes to the unfiltered findAll rather than an equals-empty query, because the vet match is whole-name equality, not prefix.
derived query as the query mechanism; the keyword choice (StartingWith vs equals+IgnoreCase) IS the prefix-vs-whole-name contract.

risks.risk: Caching the filtered query on an unvalidated user-supplied specialty string would grow the already-unevicted vets cache with arbitrary keys.
risks.mitigation: Do not annotate the filtered query methods with @Cacheable; the seeded dataset is tiny so an uncached read per filtered request is negligible. Recorded in the ADR consequences.

risks.risk: IgnoreCase must hold on all three vendors, unlike owner search which relies on per-vendor collation (a Known Defect).
risks.mitigation: The IgnoreCase derived keyword emits a vendor-neutral upper(...) comparison; it does not inherit the collation divergence. The H2 default test suite exercises the match, and the vendor-neutrality is by construction.

risks.risk: Behavior for a repeated or multi-valued specialty parameter is left unspecified (per the prd-entry non-goals).
risks.mitigation: Bind a single String; Spring MVC takes the first value. Do not add handling the requirement does not ask for.

notes: ADR written: docs/adr/2026-08-24-specialty-filter-realization.md (architectural, the how). Durable-memory writes: docs/system-design.md Contracts Implements columns (VetController/VetRepository/Vets -> REQ-VET-003) and removal of the retired /vets Known-Defects row; docs/adr/README.md index gains rows for both the non-goal ADR (the product-requirements-expert hand-off item) and this new architectural ADR. Distinct on the derived query guards against join duplication and is harmless when a vet holds a specialty once. No autofix records to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Specialty filter reaches a Spring Data derived query (findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase) that binds the argument as a query parameter; no JPQL/SQL string concatenation, so the input is not injectable.

Reflected-XSS boundary is sound: the user-controlled specialty reaches vetList.html only as a Thymeleaf link-expression query-parameter value (@{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}), which URL-encodes param values, with default HTML attribute escaping; it is never emitted via th:utext or as raw HTML text.

Cache-key-growth reasoning verified and correct: only the findAll variants are @Cacheable("vets"); both filtered derived queries are deliberately uncached, so unvalidated user input never becomes a cache key.
No path traversal, unsafe deserialization, or file I/O introduced; /vets serializes a server-built Vets wrapper and the input is a single bound String.
normalizeSpecialty maps null/blank/whitespace to null (unfiltered path) without trusting the input in any security-sensitive sink.
No dependency or build-file changes in the change set; no new supply-chain surface.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD AC [REQ-VET-003]: 'given a specialty name differing from a held specialty only by letter case, when either surface is requested for it, then it matches; given only the start of a specialty name, then it does not match.' The test theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchWholeNameCaseInsensitively covers the HTML surface only. No test exercises the JSON surface (/vets?specialty=Radiology) to verify the same case-insensitive routing. The controller's JSON path goes through the same normalizeSpecialty and findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase call, but a test is required to hold that contract against regression.

PRD AC [REQ-VET-003]: 'given a specialty that no veterinarian holds, when either surface is requested for it, then an empty directory is returned in the normal structure, not an error.' The test anUnheldSpecialtyShouldReturnAnEmptyDirectory covers the HTML surface only. The JSON surface (/vets?specialty=surgery) returning an empty vetList in the normal Vets JSON structure is not tested.

PRD AC [REQ-VET-003]: 'given an empty or whitespace-only specialty, when either surface is requested with it, then it is treated as no filter and the full directory is returned.' The test aBlankSpecialtyShouldBehaveAsNoFilter covers the HTML surface only. The JSON surface (/vets?specialty=   ) returning the full directory is not tested. The verify(never) guard on the filtered query is also absent for the JSON surface.
